claims.question: q1
claims.claim: ATANT v1.0 defined continuity as a system property with 7 required properties and introduced a 10-checkpoint, LLM-free evaluation methodology validated on a 250-story corpus.
claims.quote: ATANT v1.0 ([arXiv:2604.06710](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06710)) defined continuity as a system property with 7 required properties and introduced a 10-checkpoint, LLM-free evaluation methodology validated on a 250-story corpus.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The paper positions ATANT against a set of memory evaluations: LOCOMO, LongMemEval, BEAM, MemoryBench, Zep's evaluation suite, Letta/MemGPT's evaluations, and RULER.
claims.quote: a recurring reviewer and practitioner question has concerned not the framework itself but its relationship to a wider set of memory evaluations: LOCOMO, LongMemEval, BEAM, MemoryBench, Zep's evaluation suite, Letta/MemGPT's evaluations, and RULER.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Structural analysis shows none of these benchmarks measures continuity as defined in ATANT v1.0; median coverage is 1 of 7 required properties, mean coverage is 0.43 with partial credit at 0.5, and no eval covers more than 2 properties.
claims.quote: We show by structural analysis that none of these benchmarks measures continuity as defined in v1.0: of the 7 required properties, the median existing eval covers 1 property, the mean covers 0.43 when partial credit is scored at 0.5, and no eval covers more than 2.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The paper identifies methodological defects specific to each benchmark, including an empty-gold scoring bug in the LOCOMO reference implementation that renders 23% of its corpus unscorable by construction.
claims.quote: We provide a cell-by-cell property-coverage matrix, identify methodological defects specific to each benchmark (including an empty-gold scoring bug in the LOCOMO reference implementation that renders 23% of its corpus unscorable by construction), and publish our reference implementation's LOCOMO score (8.8%) alongside the structural reason that number is uninformative about continuity.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The authors' reference implementation scores 8.8% on LOCOMO and 96% on ATANT cumulative-scale, an 87-point divergence, which they present as evidence the benchmarks measure different properties.
claims.quote: We publish our 8.8% LOCOMO score alongside our 96% ATANT cumulative-scale score as a calibration pair: the 87-point divergence is evidence that the two benchmarks measure different properties, not that one system is an order of magnitude better than another.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The paper claims no existing benchmark can adjudicate continuity, and conflating them with continuity evaluation has led the field to under-invest in the properties ATANT v1.0 names.
claims.quote: The claim is that none of them can adjudicate continuity, and conflating them with continuity evaluation has led the field to under-invest in the properties v1.0 names.
